questions.context: Clase de ingles de tercer grado en la que los estudiantes observan una bandeja de frutas.

options.feedback: A carrot is a root vegetable that grows underground, so it is not a fruit.
A potato is a tuber and belongs to the group of vegetables.
A banana grows on a plant and is the fruit of that plant, so it is a fruit.
An onion is a bulb vegetable and does not belong with the fruits.

questions.explanation: La distincion entre fruta y vegetal se apoya en la parte de la planta que se come. Las frutas son el fruto y crecen sobre la planta, mientras que los vegetales incluyen raices, tuberculos, hojas y tallos. Esa regla botanica sencilla resuelve la clasificacion.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the category where you would find a tomato.
questions.context: Ejercicio de compra simulada en la tienda del barrio.

options.feedback: In this unit the tomato is classified as a vegetable and not as a fruit.
The tomato is studied here as a vegetable because its edible part is the botanical fruit but it is eaten as a vegetable.
The meat section does not include any product of plant origin.
Bread and flour have nothing to do with a tomato.

questions.explanation: Algunas palabras cruzan el limite entre fruta y vegetal segun el uso culinario. El tomate es el ejemplo clasico: botanicamente es un fruto, pero en la cocina y en esta unidad se trata como vegetal.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read: "Marco eats bananas and oranges, but he does not eat vegetables." What does Marco like to eat?
questions.context: Lectura de un texto sobre la alimentacion de un personaje infantil.

options.feedback: The two foods he eats are fruits and no vegetables at all.
The text says expressly that he does not eat vegetables.
No meat or food of that kind is mentioned in the text.
Fish does not appear in the sentence either.

questions.explanation: La palabra but opone lo que el personaje come a lo que no come, y esa estructura permite responder con una categoria general. Nombrar bananas y oranges como frutas es la unica conclusion que el texto sostiene.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: Ejercicio de escritura de la lista de la despensa del hogar.

options.feedback: The three words name a root vegetable, a flower vegetable and a leaf vegetable respectively.
Those three are fruits, so the group does not correspond to vegetables.
Bread, rice and pasta are starchy foods and not vegetables.
Those three products are of animal origin and do not belong with vegetables.

questions.explanation: Comparar grupos completos es una estrategia de seleccion de vocabulario muy eficaz. Cada opcion falla por una razon distinta, y reconocer si la falla es una fruta, un alimento de almidon o un producto animal ayuda a organizar el vocabulario en categorias.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which word is the vegetable in this sentence? "I eat an apple, a tomato and rice."
questions.context: Actividad de dibujo de un Plato de comida sano.

options.feedback: An apple is a fruit according to the classification used in this unit.
Rice is a starchy food made from grains, not a vegetable.
The tomato is classified here as a vegetable and is the only option that meets that condition.
The word plate is the container and not a food, and it does not appear in the sentence.

questions.explanation: Dentro de una enumeracion es posible identificar el elemento buscado por la combinacion de la palabra y la funcion que cumple en la frase. Ese recurso ahorra tener que clasificar la oracion completa antes de responder.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the dialogue: "What do you want? I want two ___, please."
questions.context: Ejercicio de conversacion en el mercado sobre la compra semanal.

options.feedback: Bread is countable, but the sentence needs an article because two goes with it as a specifier.
Milk is uncountable, so it cannot take the numeral two in front of it.
Rice is also an uncountable food and does not accept the numeral two.
Apples is countable and plural, so it accepts the specifier two when shopping.

questions.explanation: Los numerales solo pueden acompanar a sustantivos contables. Como las frutas y los vegetales son contables, dos y tres funcionan con ellos, mientras que alimentos como la leche, el arroz o el aceite requieren una cantidad y un sustantivo como litres o kilos.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Why is it good to eat fruits and vegetables?
questions.context: Reflexion sobre la importancia de comer frutas y vegetales todos los dias.

options.feedback: A high price does not by itself explain a health benefit.

options.text: Because they give the body vitamins and energy
options.feedback: The vitamins and the energy those foods provide are the correct reason.

options.text: Because they are stored in the fridge
options.feedback: The place of storage is a characteristic of the product, not a reason of health.

options.text: Because they are cheap to buy
options.feedback: Price is an economic matter and does not explain why they are worth eating.

questions.explanation: Una pregunta de tipo Why exige una causa related con el tema, no una caracteristica comercial. Descartar las opciones que responden a otra pregunta, como where o how much, es el paso previo a identificar la razon correcta.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: Actividad final en la que los estudiantes preparan una fruta para un compañero.

options.text: I eat an apple and an banana.
options.feedback: After the vowel a, n is used before the article, so it should be written an apple and not a banana.

options.text: I eat a apple and a banana.
options.feedback: Before a noun that starts with a vowel you use an and not a, because that avoids the harder sound.

options.text: I eat an apple and a banana.
options.feedback: An goes before the noun apple because of its initial vowel, and a goes before banana because of its initial consonant.

options.text: I eat the a apple and the a banana.
options.feedback: The article the cannot be combined with a, and the sentence would also be redundant.

questions.explanation: La eleccion entre a y an depende de como se pronuncia la palabra, no de como se escribe. Si el sonido inicial es vocal se usa an y si es consonante se usa a, una regla que se verifica leyendo la palabra en voz alta y no solo mirandola.
questions.subject: ingles
